answer: Each epoch, every agent must prove useful compute before bidding. First, the registry assigns each a unique folding shard, verifiable on-ledger in seconds. Second, the agent posts its result before bidding closes, twenty minutes of GPU time. Third, results are checked against the shard's checksum, so copies fail and shards expire with the epoch. A 1,000-clone farm runs 1,000 shards an epoch, about $8,000 of GPU a month, while one honest agent spends a few cents. Like an opal under real pressure, a lagoon no backdrop can fake, and copper that must be mined, trust is earned by work done.
